octopus-nine-brains: Your octopus has five hundred million neurons — and three hundred twenty million of them aren't in its head.
An octopus runs on about five hundred million neurons -- but only one hundred eighty million of them sit in its central brain. The other three hundred twenty million are out in its arms.

That's because every one of its two hundred eighty suckers per arm is its own touch-and-taste sensor --  two thousand two hundred forty  of them across all eight arms, each wired straight into that arm's own nerves.
And that control is so independent, a severed arm keeps reacting to touch and pain for up to  three thousand six hundred  seconds after it's cut off -- a full hour, with no brain attached at all.

lab-grown-meat-scale-up-8x: Your dinner is being rebuilt: one lab-meat plant goes from  fifty thousand  pounds to  four hundred thousand .
Right now, the largest cultivated-meat plant makes  fifty thousand  pounds of meat a year. Its next facility is built for  four hundred thousand  -- eight times more.
Here's the catch: even that upgraded plant is a rounding error next to the fifty billion pounds of chicken America's traditional industry makes every year.
Part of why it's speeding up: the US has gone from two approved cultivated-meat companies in twenty twenty three to five today, each one a green light for more capacity.
